§ 3MAKING OF CONSTITUTION

Committees of the Constituent Assembly

  • The Constituent Assembly of India formed 8 Major and 13 Minor committees.

Major Committee of Constituent Assembly

CommitteeHead
Union Powers CommitteeJ. L. Nehru
Union Constitution CommitteeJ. L. Nehru
States CommitteeJ. L. Nehru
Provincial Constitution CommitteeSardar Patel
Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, and Tribal and Excluded AreasSardar Patel
Drafting CommitteeDr. B. R. Ambedkar
Rules of Procedure CommitteeDr. Rajendra Prasad
Steering CommitteeDr. Rajendra Prasad

Minor Committee of Constituent Assembly

CommitteeHead
Finance and Staff CommitteeDr. Rajendra Prasad
Ad-hoc Committee on the National FlagDr. Rajendra Prasad
Credentials CommitteeAlladi Krishnaswami Ayyar
House CommitteeB. Pattabhi Sitaramayya
Committee on Chief Commissioners ProvincesB. Pattabhi Sitaramayya
Order of Business CommitteeDr. K. M. Munshi
Committee on the Functions of the Constituent AssemblyG. V. Mavalankar
Ad-hoc Committee on the Supreme CourtS. Varadachariar
Ad-hoc Committee CitizenshipS. Varadachariar
Expert Committee on the Financial Provisions of the Union ConstitutionNalini Ranjan Sarkar
Linguistic Provinces CommissionS. K. Dhar
Special Committee to Examine the Draft ConstitutionJ. L. Nehru
Press Gallery CommitteeUsha Nath Sen

DRAFTING COMMITTEE

  • Set up on: 29th August 1947
  • Total members of Drafting Committee: 7
  • Chairman: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar (also known as "Modern Manu" or "Modern Man")
  • Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar
  • N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar
  • Syed Muhammad Saadulla
  • B. L. Mitter (replaced by N. Madhav Rau)
  • D. P. Khaitan (replaced by T. T. Krishnamachari)
  • K. M. Munshi

Drafts of Constituent Assembly

  • 21 Feb 1948: First draft was published. It took 8 months for people of India to discuss.
  • 4 Nov 1948: B. R. Ambedkar introduced the final draft before Constituent Assembly.
B. R. Ambedkar was elected to the Constituent Assembly from Bengal in July 1946 (before Partition) but after Partition he was elected from Bombay Presidency.
  • 1st reading: 5 days (4th Nov 1948-9th Nov 1948).
  • 2nd reading: 10 months and 3 days (15 Nov 1948-17 Oct 1949)
  • 3rd reading: Completed on 26 Nov 1949.

Important Sections

  • Total sessions held: 11 sessions for 165 days.
  • Total time taken for drafting the Constitution: 2 years 11 months 18 days.
  • Budget: 64 lakhs (to frame the Constitution).
  • 1st Session: 9-23rd December 1946
  • 10th Session: 6-17th October 1949
  • 11th Session: 14-26th November 1949 (also the last session).
  • Final Draft: Presented by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar before the public on 4th November 1948.
  • 26th November 1949: Constitution was adopted (this day is also celebrated as the "Constitution Day")
  • 26th November 1949: Some provisions were imposed:
  • Citizenship (Article 5-9)
  • Elections (Article 324-329)
  • Provisional Parliament
  • 26th January 1950: Constitution was enforced / commenced on this day. Hence, this day is celebrated as THE REPUBLIC DAY OF INDIA.
  • The reason for choosing this date is because on the same day in 1930 Purna Swaraj day was celebrated following the Lahore session (1929)
Originally, our Constitution consisted of 395 Articles, 8 Schedules, 22 Parts and a Preamble.

Functions of the Constituent Assembly

  • It acted as a law-making body (to legislate) → G. V. Mavalankar (first speaker of Lok Sabha)
  • It acted as a Constitution making body.
  • Temporary President (before elections): Sachchidananda Sinha
  • President (after elections): Rajendra Prasad
  • Vice President: V. T. Krishnamachari and H. C. Mukherjee
  • It functioned as the 'First Parliament of India.'
  • It adopted National Flag on 22 July, 1947
  • It adopted National Anthem ("Jana Gana Mana" → by Rabindranath Tagore) and National Song ("Vande Matram" → by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee) on 24 January, 1950.
  • It ratified India's membership of the Commonwealth in May 1949.
  • Elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the 1st President of India on 26 Jan 1950.

Some more Significant facts to know:

  • Legal / Constitutional advisor: B. N. Rau
  • Chief Draftsman: S. N. Mukherjee

§ 4MAKING OF CONSTITUTION

  • No. of members who signed constitution: 284 (including 15 female members)
  • Signed on the last sitting of the Constituent Assembly on 24 Jan 1950.
  • Constitution Calligraphers:
  • English: Prem Bihari Narain Raizada
  • Hindi: Vasant Krishan Vaidya
  • Constitution decorator: Nand Lal Bose and Beohar Rammanohar Sinha
  • Secretary of Constituent Assembly: H.V. Iyengar
  • India's constitution is the largest written constitution, its symbol is an Elephant.
  • Language of the Constitution: English

Important Female members of The Constituent Assembly

  • Rajkumari Amrit Kaur → 1st Health minister
  • Sucheta Kriplani → 1st female Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh
  • Sarojini Naidu → 1st Governor of Uttar Pradesh
